name: Electric dew pump
subtitle: pulls water from dry air without heating

effects.effect: water vapour condenses inside tiny pores before the air is saturated
a voltage across a wet porous material makes the liquid flow

effect: water vapour condenses inside tiny pores before the air is saturated
how: Desert air holds water even when it is far too dry for dew, but most harvesters must heat their sponge to get the water back out, which wastes energy. Here water condenses inside the tiny pores of a ceramic sheet even at low humidity (capillary condensation), and a solar-powered voltage across the sheet pushes it straight through the pores to drip out the far side (electro-osmosis).
obstacle: Water in such tiny pores is held so tightly that pushing it out may take as much electricity as heating would.
why: Steady water from dry air with no heating step would help billions in water-scarce regions.
real: US patent 7709129 describes capillary condensation of vapour in a flow passage with the condensed water moved out by electro-osmosis; no working humidity harvester of this kind found.
